subject: Mid-contract expansion: stepwise top-up + invoice split / co-term
messages:
From: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@alphamed.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alphamed Procurement <procurement@alphamed.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:18 -0700
Subject: Request: mid-contract top-up + co-term options

Hi Marcus,

We had a spike in demand across our imaging workflows and are looking to increase our committed units by ~40% effective immediately. Our contract runs through 2027-12-31 and procurement has asked whether we can: 1) do a mid-contract top-up that co-terms to our existing renewal date, and 2) split the invoice (partial now / remainder at co-term) to align budgets.

High level requirements from procurement:
- Co-term the added capacity to 2027-12-31
- Prefer a staged payment (we can do 60/40 or 50/50)
- Need a simple amendment they can sign within 2–3 weeks
- Any uplift discount you'd be willing to offer for committing to the larger run-rate?

I attached our Q3 usage snapshot for context (usage-report-q3.csv). Can you share options (pricing paths + timelines)? If helpful, I can coordinate a short call this week with our procurement lead.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Zhang
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
Alphamed Inc.

[attachment: usage-report-q3.csv]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Zhang <c.zhang@alphamed.com>
Cc: Alphamed Procurement <procurement@alphamed.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:45:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract top-up + co-term options

Hi Claire — thanks for the context and the usage file. Good news: we have two straightforward paths that should meet procurement needs; I describe the trade-offs below. I can join procurement for a 30-min call tomorrow if that helps finalize timing.

Option 1 — Immediate top-up (prorated)
- Add the 40% capacity now, prorated to your co-term date (billed for 9 months of additional capacity).
- One invoice now for the prorated period.
- Discount: 7% off list for the incremental units if you pick immediate billing.
- Pros: Fast activation, simple amendment.
- Cons: Higher up-front cash impact.

Option 2 — Stepwise voucher + co-term annualize (recommended for budget smoothing)
- We stage the increase: deploy full capacity now, but convert part of the initial spend into vouchers that convert to committed units at co-term.
- Invoice split: example 60% now / 40% at co-term (we can match your preference).
- Discount: 10% if you annualize the augmented run-rate at co-term (i.e., commit to the new capacity through 2027-12-31).
- Pros: Lower effective blended price, smoother procurement.
- Cons: Requires a short amendment and a co-term acceptance by your procurement team.

Additional notes:
- We can include a 95th percentile latency exception at your request for a modest SLA addendum (need legal review).
- We can set the retention window per your compliance needs; if you need extended retention we may need a small storage surcharge.

I attached a short one-pager that lays out the two options and sample invoice split scenarios (marcus_proposal_options.pdf). Let me know which path you prefer and I’ll draft an amendment for procurement/legal review.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

[attachment: marcus_proposal_options.pdf]

Subject: Re: Request: mid-contract top-up + co-term options

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear options. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and security:

- Procurement: prefers Option 2 (stepwise voucher) but wants 10% discount to justify the amended commit internally. They also prefer a 60/40 split.
- Security/Compliance: Can Redwood commit to a short SLA carveout for 95th percentile latency for our critical inference route? Also need confirmation that audit logs and KMS usage will be preserved for 12 months for the added capacity.
- Invoicing: they want the amendment to support a PO workflow and to show the two-line split on the first invoice.

I’ve attached our standard procurement checklist for amendments (procurement_requirements.docx). Can you confirm you can meet the SLA/retention asks and whether Redwood can do 10% on Option 2? If 10% is doable we can move to draft amendment and I’ll loop our procurement lead to execute.

Claire

Invoice formatting: finance can output the first invoice with two line items ("Top-up: prorated months" and "Voucher: deferred credit") and a second invoice at co-term for the remaining committed portion. We will include a reference PO field.
